hints: The smallest key is at the far-left end of the tree. After you hand it out, where is the next smallest key?
Simulate an in-order traversal one step at a time with a stack. Keep the left spine of unvisited nodes on the stack; the top is always the next key.

1. Constructor: push root and all its left descendants.
  2. next(): pop the top node.
  3. Push the popped node's right child and all of that child's left descendants.
  4. Return the popped value.
  5. hasNext(): return whether the stack is non-empty.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Do a full in-order walk in the constructor, store all keys in a list, and hand them out with an index.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Lazy in-order with a stack holding only one root-to-leaf path's worth of nodes.

explain: For the tree [5,2,9], the constructor pushes 5 then 2. next() pops 2 (no right child) and returns 2; the next next() pops 5, pushes its right child 9, and returns 5. hasNext() is true since 9 is on the stack, next() returns 9, and then hasNext() is false. Each node is pushed and popped exactly once, so the total work over all calls is O(n), which is O(1) per call on average.
recognize: "Return keys one at a time in sorted order, using O(height) memory" → controlled in-order traversal with a stack.
